'''Shayne Mitchell Whittington''' (born March 27, 1991) is an American-Macedonian former professional [[basketball]] player who currently serves as an assistant coach for the [[Western Michigan Broncos men's basketball|Western Michigan Broncos]]. He also represents [[Macedonia national basketball team|North Macedonia]] in the international competitions. He played college basketball for [[Western Michigan Broncos men's basketball|Western Michigan University]].

==High school career==
Whittington attended Lawrence High School in [[Lawrence, Michigan]]. As a junior, he averaged 11.3 points, 9.2 rebounds and 2.1 blocks per game, leading Lawrence to a 23–2 record and earning Detroit Free Press Class D Honorable Mention All-State honors.<ref name=bio>{{cite web|url=http://www.wmubroncos.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=4600&ATCLID=204772315|title=#21 Shayne Whittington|website=wmubroncos.com|accessdate=July 6, 2014}}</ref>

As a senior, he averaged 17.2 points, 12.1 rebounds, 4.0 blocks, 3.0 steals and 2.0 assists per game as the Tigers went 24–2, a school record for wins. He was named Class D First Team All-State by Bankhoops.com, BCAM, Detroit News, Detroit Free Press and Associated Press.<ref name="bio" />

==College career==
In his freshman season at [[Western Michigan Broncos men's basketball|Western Michigan]], Whittington played sparingly for the Broncos. In 16 games, he averaged 1.4 points and 1.6 rebounds in 5.9 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name=stats>{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/shayne-whittington-1.html|title=Shayne Whittington Stats|work=Sports-Reference.com|accessdate=July 6, 2014}}</ref>

In November 2010, Whittington elected to redshirt the 2010–11 season after finding himself behind freshman Matt Stainbrook and junior Caleb Dean in the team's rotation.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/broncos/index.ssf/2010/11/western_michigans_mens_basketb_1.html|title=Western Michigan's men's basketball team spreads minutes around in exhibition win over Kalamazoo College|work=MLive.com|date=November 6, 2010|accessdate=July 6, 2014}}</ref>

On November 12, 2011, Whittington played his first game since the 2009–10 season at South Dakota State, recording three points and two rebounds in 10 minutes of action. In his redshirted sophomore season, he played 32 games (7 starts), averaging 4.2 points and 4.0 rebounds in 14.1 minutes per game.

In his junior season, he was named to the 2013 All-MAC second team and led the conference with 12 double-doubles. In 35 games (all starts), he averaged 13.2 points, 8.8 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.7 blocks in 29.7 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his senior season, he was named to the 2014 All-MAC first team after being named the MAC West Player of the Week four times. In 31 games (all starts), he averaged 16.1 points, 8.9 rebounds, 1.1 assists and 1.5 blocks in 31.8 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

==Professional career==

===Indiana Pacers (2014–2016)===
Whittington went undrafted in the [[2014 NBA draft]]. On July 2, 2014, he signed with the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-sign-shayne-whittington|title=Pacers Sign Shayne Whittington|work=NBA.com|date=July 2, 2014|accessdate=July 6, 2014}}</ref> On November 8, he made his NBA debut in a 97–90 loss to the [[Washington Wizards]], recording two points, three rebounds and two assists in eight minutes off the bench.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141108/WASIND/gameinfo.html|title=Wall, Nene lead Wizards over Pacers 97–90|work=NBA.com|date=November 8, 2014|accessdate=March 20, 2016}}</ref> On January 28, 2015, he was assigned to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Shayne Whittington Assigned to NBA D-League|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/shayne-whittington-assigned-nba-d-league|date=January 28, 2015|accessdate=December 28, 2015|work=NBA.com}}</ref> He was recalled by the Pacers two days later.<ref>{{cite news|title=Shayne Whittington Recalled From NBA D-League|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/shayne-whittington-recalled-nba-d-league|date=January 30, 2015|accessdate=December 28, 2015|work=NBA.com}}</ref> On April 8, he was reassigned to the Mad Ants to help the team in their playoff run.<ref>{{cite news|title=Shayne Whittington Assigned to NBA D-League's Fort Wayne Mad Ants|url=http://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/?id=4948715|date=April 8, 2015|accessdate=December 28, 2015|work=OurSportsCentral.com}}</ref> He returned to the Pacers in late April following the Mad Ants' 2–0 D-League Finals series loss to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Hotchkiss|first=Wheat|title=Whittington's Season Comes to End|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/whittingtons-season-comes-end|date=April 27, 2015|accessdate=December 28, 2015|work=NBA.com}}</ref>

On July 27, 2015, Whittington re-signed with the Pacers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/pacers-re-sign-whittington-and-sign-christmas-and-robinson|title=Pacers Re-Sign Whittington and Sign Christmas and Robinson|date=July 27, 2015|work=NBA.com|accessdate=July 27, 2015}}</ref> During the 2015–16 season, he received multiple assignments to the Fort Wayne Mad Ants.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |title=2015–16 NBA Assignments |work=NBA.com |accessdate=January 25, 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150906020056/http://dleague.nba.com/news/assignments/ |archivedate=September 6, 2015 }}</ref> That offseason, he was waived by the Pacers.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-whittington|title=Pacers Waive Whittington|date=July 29, 2016|work=NBA.com|accessdate=July 29, 2016}}</ref>

===Obradoiro CAB (2016–2017)===
Whittington signed with [[Obradoiro CAB|Río Natura Monbus Obradoiro]] of Spain's [[Liga ACB]] on August 7, 2016.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=124712|title=Shayne Whittington, un pívot NBA para el Rio Natura Monbus Obradoiro|work=ACB.com|date=August 7, 2016|accessdate=August 7, 2016|language=Spanish|archive-date=August 10, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160810193608/http://www.acb.com/redaccion.php?id=124712|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Zenit Saint Petersburg (2017–2018)===
On July 21, 2017, Whittington signed with Russian club [[B.C. Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit Saint Petersburg]] for the 2017–18 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Zenit landed center Whittington|url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/7ym6vtoxj787xskp|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170722183806/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/7ym6vtoxj787xskp|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 22, 2017|accessdate=July 21, 2017|work=Eurocupbasketball.com|date=July 21, 2017}}</ref>

===MoraBanc Andorra (2018)===
On July 26, 2018, Whittington signed a two-year deal with [[BC Andorra|MoraBanc Andorra]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Andorra bolsters frontcourt with Whittington |url=http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8wf6idjwdlnjmtal |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180726135218/http://www.eurocupbasketball.com/eurocup/news/i/8wf6idjwdlnjmtal |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 26, 2018 |accessdate=July 26, 2018 |work=EuroCupBasketball.com |date=July 26, 2018}}</ref>

===Movistar Estudiantes (2018–2019)===
On December 27, 2018, Whittington signed with [[CB Estudiantes|Movistar Estudiantes]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/estudiantes-officially-signs-shayne-whittington/|title=Estudiantes officially signs Shayne Whittington|website=Sportando|access-date=January 6, 2019|archive-date=July 26, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190726230734/https://sportando.basketball/en/estudiantes-officially-signs-shayne-whittington/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Coosur Real Betis (2019–2020)===
On August 1, 2019, Whittington signed a two-year deal with [[Real Betis Baloncesto|Coosur Real Betis]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Shayne Whittington signs with Real Betis Sevilla |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/shayne-whittington-signs-with-real-betis-sevilla/ |accessdate=1 August 2019 |work=Sportando |date=1 August 2019}}</ref> He averaged 8 points and 4 rebounds per game. On June 9, 2020, Whittington parted ways with the team.<ref>{{cite news |title=Real Betis, Shayne Whittington part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/real-betis-shayne-whittington-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |accessdate=June 9, 2020 |date=June 9, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

==Coaching career==
===Indiana Pacers===
On June 2, 2023, Whittington became an assistant coach for the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Agness|title=Former Pacer added to staff|url=https://www.fieldhousefiles.com/p/former-pacer-shayne-whittington-added-to-staff|work=FieldhouseFiles.com|date=June 2, 2023|access-date=July 26, 2023}}</ref>

===College===
===Western Michigan===
On June 19, 2024, Whittington was hired by his alma mater [[Western Michigan Broncos men's basketball|Western Michigan]] as an assistant coach.<ref>{{cite web|first=Scott|last=Agness|title=Shayne Whittington has been hired as an assistant coach at his alma mater, Western Michigan|url= https://x.com/scottagness/status/1803583928046915952?s=46&t=hcA_ZpjXERy-BRTMkG8GZw|work=X.com|date=June 19, 2024|access-date=June 19, 2024}}</ref>

Whittington is the son of Scott Whittington and Carrie Rokos, and has one older brother, Spencer, a younger sister, Erika, and two younger brothers, Cody and Joey.<ref name="bio" />
